answer: Each identity claims one basalt ridge post, lights its lantern, locks an 80-credit bond, and files a log: elevation, fuel burned, visibility range. An auditor recomputes the range from the ridge visibility table; a mismatch beyond 5 percent, a reused log, or one key on two posts burns the bond. First filing 39; the kth under one key costs 39 plus 7 times k minus 1, so the 1000th costs 7032 and 1000 fakes pay 3,535,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-lantern ring fails: its log bears the lender key and mismatches the borrower's elevation. An honest agent pays 39 once, bond returned after audit.
